desc:
Privacy and consent for product recommendations means your suggestion tools only use shopper data in the way your cookie banner and privacy page say they do. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your tools, sets them to wait for consent and tests what happens when a visitor declines.

## Why recommendations raise a privacy question

Personalized suggestions work by remembering what a visitor viewed, clicked or bought. That memory is often stored through cookies or similar identifiers. Without care, a recommendation script can start collecting data before the visitor has made any choice.

This creates two risks. Shoppers may feel watched, and you may fall out of line with the rules that apply in the places you sell to. A clear setup protects trust, and trust is part of what makes suggestions work at all.

## What is consent setup for recommendation tools?

Consent setup for recommendation tools is the work of connecting your suggestion scripts to your cookie banner, so they run only when the visitor has allowed the relevant category. It also covers what the store shows when the visitor says no, usually a set of non personal items such as best sellers.

## How clear consent affects the store

A well-built consent flow does not have to hurt the shopping experience. Visitors who accept see personalized blocks. Visitors who decline still see useful products, because the fallback shows popular or new items instead of an empty gap.

Good wording matters too. A banner that explains in plain language what suggestions do tends to feel honest, and a clear privacy page answers questions before they become complaints. We are not lawyers and this service is not legal advice, so we hand you a checklist your own adviser can review.

## What a careful setup includes

- A list of every tool and script that uses shopper data for suggestions.
- A check of what runs before consent is given.
- Recommendation scripts set to wait for the right consent category.
- A tested decline path, with non personal items as the fallback.
- Plain wording for your cookie banner.
- A short line in your privacy page that describes recommendations.
- A data map of what is collected, where it goes and why.
- A review of regional settings where you sell.
- An opt out link where your tools support one.
- A checklist for your adviser.

## How we work

We begin by scanning your store for tools that touch shopper data, including recommendation apps, email tools, analytics and ad pixels that feed suggestions. We record what each one sets and when.

Next we connect the relevant tools to your existing consent banner, using the settings that banner provides. We then test as a visitor who accepts, one who declines and one who ignores the banner, and write down what happened in each case. We do not replace your cookie banner app unless you ask, and we work with the one you have.

Basic covers the tool list, wording drafts and a check of what runs early. Standard adds consent wiring, decline testing and a privacy page line. Premium adds the data map, a regional review, opt out links where supported, an adviser checklist and a walkthrough call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a written list of every tool that uses shopper data.
- Give visitors a real choice in the banner.
- Show a sensible fallback to people who decline.
- Retest after you add or update any app.
- Ask a qualified adviser to review your final wording.

**Avoid:**
- Loading personalization scripts before consent where it is needed.
- Copying privacy wording that does not match your tools.
- Assuming one banner setting covers every region.
- Hiding the decline option.
- Treating this service as legal advice.

## Who this is for

This service suits stores that sell to visitors in several countries, stores about to add personalization and owners who have noticed that scripts fire before the banner is answered. It also suits teams that need a clear record to share with a legal or compliance adviser.

## What we need from you

Send a list of the apps and tools you use, and tell us where your customers live. Give us access as a collaborator, staff or developer user, never a password. Share the name of your cookie banner tool. We tell you what we find before we change any settings.
